messages:
Eli (support): FYI customer 'Maplytics' opened an escalation — embeddings throughput dropped ~4x around 12:45 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec tanked. Also seeing intermittent 400s with \"dimension mismatch\" in logs.
Maria (ml-eng): :eyes: can you paste a sample request/response and the request size distribution?
Eli (support): sending logs below. sample curl that hit the 400: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v2","inputs":["short text","longer text 1","longer text 2"]}'
```
response: `{"error":{"message":"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768","type":"invalid_request"}}`
Nguyen (infra): Thanks. I see a token rotation completed at 12:44:58 UTC (deploy-bot below). Could be a client using an older model variant key?
deploy-bot: Token rotation job `rot-2026-03-17-1244` finished: rotated service tokens for embed-pool-3, no rollback.
Cassie (sre): Also noticing GPU queue depth spike on pool embed-pool-3 starting 12:46 — queue depth went from ~30 -> 220, latency & head-of-queue increases.
Jules (support): Any billing/auth errors? customer reported some 402s earlier.
Eli (support): Yeah a few 402 billing errors at 12:47, possibly due to token mismatches.
Maria (ml-eng): Hypothesis: some clients got new token that maps to a different default model variant (quantized 768-dim variant) but request payload still expects 1536-dim outputs -> dimension mismatch. The throughput drop could be due to automatic fallback logic thrashing between model variants causing cache/KV misses and increased batching inefficiency.
Arjun (eng-runtime): Repro attempt on staging: I rotated a token to map to a 768-dim variant while sending 1536-dim expectation -> immediate 400s. If many requests hit mixed model variants, runtime tries to recompile kernels and queues stall.
Nguyen (infra): Repro logs (trimmed): 
```
[12:46:01] pool embed-pool-3: enqueue request id=abc size=1536 -> schedule model embed-lite-v2-quant-768
[12:46:01] runtime: model mismatch -> fallback to embed-lite-v2-1536
[12:46:02] gpu-queue: saturating (depth=220)
```
Eli (support): Customer repro steps: running the curl with 10k requests concurrently reproduced the drop.
Cassie (sre): Short mitigation: pin affected customer to a stable model variant (1536) and throttle concurrent inflight requests. I'll add a per-customer concurrency cap for the pool.
Maria (ml-eng): Also recommend adding a quick server-side validation that rejects requests if token->model mapping doesn't match requested output dim with a clearer error (and no fallback thrash).
Jules (support): I can patch the customer creds to the pinned variant and confirm if their errors stop.
Eli (support): Doing now. Patch applied at 12:54.
Nguyen (infra): Rolling back the token rotation for embed-pool-3 (partial rollback) at 12:56:20 UTC.
deploy-bot: Rollback action `rot-2026-03-17-1244` initiated by Nguyen; status: success.
Cassie (sre): After rollback: queue depth dropping back to ~40 within 3 minutes, vectors/sec trending to baseline.
Eli (support): Customer confirms: vectors/sec recovered and 400s stopped. They still saw 402 billing spike for a handful of requests but those cleared after re-auth.
Maria (ml-eng): Root cause summary for postmortem: token rotation altered token->model mapping for some tokens, causing mixed-dimension model selection for same endpoint. Runtime fallback & recompiles + KV cache cold starts produced GPU queue saturation and throughput regression.
Arjun (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) change rotation process to update token->model mapping atomically with routing metadata, 2) add fast validation to surface dimension mismatch and avoid expensive fallback, 3) add circuit-breaker to limit thrashing between variants, 4) test rotation on a canary subset with load.
Nguyen (infra): I'll add a temporary rule to the autoscaler to add burst capacity for embed-pools during future rotations.
Jules (support): I'll notify the customer of root cause and steps taken.
Eli (support): Thanks team. I'll open a postmortem doc and link to repro steps + logs. Quick note for the doc: include the curl + python repro and the infra logs.
Maria (ml-eng): Example repro python snippet for postmortem: 
```python
import requests
for i in range(10000):
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'embed-lite-v2','inputs':['a']})
  if r.status_code != 200:
    print(i, r.status_code, r.text)
```
Eli (support): Closing thread — will attach postmortem link when ready. :thumbsup:
